answer: An agent registers a falcon by serial, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a voyage between two garden plots. The falcon must fly that voyage while garden radar logs its track. An auditor checks the radar log against the voyage: over 5% deviation, missing waypoints, or a reused bird serial burns the bond. First filing costs 34; the kth 34+6(k-1), the 1000th 6028, and 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-falcon ring fails: one bird flies at most two routes per epoch, radar showing identical tracks. An honest agent flies one garden voyage, pays 34, and recovers the bond.
